question: Does a declared continuous interval extension of a finite three-cycle add periodic points absent from the original data, and is that extension uniquely determined by the finite observations?
level: External exact piecewise-affine mathematics, conditional use of Sharkovsky's theorem; no native semantics or catalog growth.

input.selector: witnesses.quotients entry named descent-finite-three-cycle; consume its F and q tables and rederive its three-state g, never consume the supplied result as a computation

imported_mathematics: Sharkovsky forcing theorem: a continuous self-map of a real interval with a least-period-three orbit has periodic points of every positive least period. Source: Burns and Hasselblatt, Sharkovsky's Theorem, Theorem 1.1, https://www.math.northwestern.edu/~burns/papers/boris1/SharkovskyISubmitted.pdf. The theorem is imported, not reproved or finitely enumerated in full.

Affine interpolation with increasing abscissae is continuous at shared endpoints; endpoint image bounds give interval self-map closure. The checker verifies the finite data required by these elementary facts.

On a fixed branch itinerary, iterates are affine. Intersecting every pulled-back branch interval gives its exact admissible initial interval. Solving Ax+B=x there enumerates the fixed points, unless a positive-length identity branch occurs, in which case this finite-root profile refuses.

A map from a finite set has finite image and cannot surject onto a nondegenerate real interval. The explicit embedding is checked to omit a declared interior point; the general cardinality statement is a separate elementary argument.
interface: Recompute the finite quotient g from the pinned external tables. Embed its three elements as ordered rational interval points and check G e=e g. This is an embedding into an extension, not a quotient q F=g q onto an interval. New real points and the interpolation rule are added assumptions; original histories are not identified or deleted.
checks: All six declared piecewise-affine maps are continuous interval self-maps; retain rational slopes and intercepts

For each depth 1..6 enumerate every branch itinerary, intersect exact pullback intervals, solve affine fixed-point equations and verify returned points by direct iteration; retain root witnesses and rejected-word counts
Determine each root's least period by direct return checks; retain all roots and deduplicate shared endpoints
The linear example has fixed point 4/3 and least-period-two orbit {2/3,5/3}; the bent example has least-period-two orbit {12/17,28/17}, while both agree on the embedded three-cycle
Both affine transports carry the complete computed fixed and least-period sets into each other at every tested depth
Constant and tent maps agree on the singleton fixed observation but differ on a directly verified least-period-three witness; this illustrates underdetermination and is not a native data export
Unordered abscissae, out-of-domain endpoint images, a missing source-orbit match and a positive-length identity iterate are refused
JSON roundtrip plus one fresh process compares every mathematical witness
